runtimeEvidence: Owner video 27/11/2026: cockpit pieces displaced in a ~3 m pass at 805 km/h over the sea, before contact.

0.2.1 pass at 805 km/h over open sea: vertical fins and nose side shells/frames lost their joints below HUD 2.8 m, the belly about 6 m above the sea (flight-waterpass-20261127-073605, flight-waterpass-wet-20261127-081114); the native water check uses each part's lift point, 9 m below the fins and 0.9 m below the wheel line for the nose (flight-waterline-lift-20261127-081305).

0.2.2 (CourierWaterline): pass held at HUD 8, 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1 and 0.5 m, 0 parts lost (flight-waterpass-022e-high-20261127-082933); descending into the sea, 0 parts lost down to the wheel line 2.5 m below the sea, first wet part the forward belly with the wheel line 2.95 m below the sea (belly at the waterline), then the native breakup (flight-waterpass-022e-contact-20261127-082848).

Root keeps the native depth once the hull is in the sea (native buoyancy after a ditching): HUD 8 to 0.5 m, 0 lost (flight-waterpass-022f-high-20261127-095208); first wet part with the belly at the waterline (flight-waterpass-022f-contact-20261127-095125).

Ditching at 100 km/h, belly brought onto the sea and released at idle: 0.2.2 stays intact and sinks at about 2.4 m/s (flight-ditch5-022-20261127-094656); 0.2.1 had lost 55 parts to water drag on the fins and nose before contact and sank at about 1.9 m/s (flight-ditch4-021-20261127-093722). Neither floats in this probe.
